source.book: Tajweed Rules of the Qur'an — Part One
source.verification: book source checked; Qur'anic references cross-checked

prerequisites: Recognize noon saakinah and all three tanween forms.
Use the routine: find the target, then inspect the next letter.
Distinguish a clear noon sound in izhar.
learningOutcomes: Define idgham as merging one letter into the next.
Name the four idgham-with-ghunnah letters: ي ن م و.
Identify the rule in at least 8 of 10 mixed boundaries.
Explain that this idgham occurs across two words.
Recite four verified examples with a merged sound and a two-count ghunnah.

linguistic.ar: الإدغام لغةً: إدخال الشيء في الشيء.
linguistic.en: Linguistically, idgham means inserting or merging one thing into another.

technical.ar: الإدغام بغنة هو إدخال النون الساكنة أو التنوين في أحد حروف ي ن م و حتى يصيرا حرفًا واحدًا مشددًا من جنس الحرف الثاني، مع غنة مقدارها حركتان.
technical.en: Idgham with ghunnah merges noon saakinah or tanween into a following ي، ن، م، or و, producing a strengthened sound of the second letter with a two-count ghunnah.

studentFriendly.ar: إذا جاء بعد النون الساكنة أو التنوين حرف من ي ن م و بين كلمتين، لا نظهر النون منفصلة؛ ندمجها في الحرف التالي مع غنة حركتين.
studentFriendly.en: When noon saakinah or tanween is followed across two words by ي، ن، م، or و, merge the noon sound into the next letter and hold the ghunnah for two counts.

definition.memoryFormula: نْ أو تنوين + ي ن م و = إدغام بغنة حركتين

keyTerms.en: merging one sound into the next
a nasal sound from the nasal passage
memory word containing ي ن م و

teacherPreparation: Prepare four trigger cards: ي ن م و.
Model clear izhar and merged idgham as an audible contrast.
Use a steady two-count hand gesture for ghunnah.
Do not rely on written transliteration as a substitute for live recitation.

openingReview.teacherPrompt: Show نْ and the three tanween forms; ask the learner to name the target.
Review izhar: does the noon remain separate or merge?
Ask the learner to read the memory word ينمو.

conceptExplanation.text: In izhar the noon remains clear and separate. In idgham with ghunnah, the noon sound joins the next letter and a controlled nasal sound remains for two counts.
Teach recognition, merging, and ghunnah timing as separate skills. This lesson covers ي ن م و across two words; the four absolute-manifestation exceptions belong to the following lesson.

lessonPath.title: Discover
lessonPath.text: Inspect the next letter: ي ن م و.

lessonPath.title: Compare
lessonPath.text: Hear clear izhar versus merged idgham.

lessonPath.title: Count
lessonPath.text: Hold the ghunnah for two balanced counts.

visualExplanation.display: نْ / ً ٍ ٌ  +  ي ن م و  ←  إدغام بغنة (حركتان)
visualExplanation.teacherUse: Point to the word boundary before modeling the merged sound.

ruleSummary.condition: Noon saakinah or tanween is followed in the next word by ي، ن، م، or و.
ruleSummary.result: Merge the noon sound into the following letter and keep a controlled ghunnah for two counts.
ruleSummary.location: In this rule, the target and trigger occur across two words.

quranExamples.arabic: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُۥ
quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge the noon into ya and hold the ghunnah for two counts before completing ya.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Ya follows noon saakinah across two words.
quranExamples.commonError: Pronouncing a separate clear noon before ya.

quranExamples.arabic: وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ
quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge into the strengthened noon and keep its ghunnah for two counts.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Noon follows noon saakinah across two words.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Move from the noon sound into the closed lips of mim with a two-count ghunnah.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Mim follows noon saakinah across two words.
quranExamples.commonError: Keeping the tongue fixed for a clear noon instead of preparing the lips for mim.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge the tanween noon sound into waw with a two-count ghunnah.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Waw follows tanween across two words.
quranExamples.commonError: Dropping the tanween sound completely without leaving the ghunnah.

guidedPractice.studentAction: Name the target, trigger, and rule.
guidedPractice.feedback: Require the learner to say that the letters are in two words.

guidedPractice.teacherAction: Model isolate → merge → two-count ghunnah → full phrase.
guidedPractice.studentAction: Copy each stage, then recite independently.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Do not keep a separate noon sound.

commonMistakes: Pronouncing a separate clear noon before the trigger.
Removing the noon sound without preserving ghunnah.
Holding the ghunnah too briefly or too long.
Applying this rule inside one word.
Confusing ينمو with the throat letters.
correctionTechniques: Contrast a deliberately clear noon with the correctly merged form.
Use two finger taps for the ghunnah timing.
Practice the boundary alone before the full phrase.
Require the learner to point to the space between the two words.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Name the four letters using ينمو.
Classify ten mixed izhar and idgham boundaries.
knowledgeChecks.success: At least eight are correct with a reason.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Recite one example for each trigger.
knowledgeChecks.success: Merging and two-count ghunnah are teacher-approved.

teacherQuestions: What letter begins the next word?
Should the noon remain separate or merge?
How many counts does the ghunnah last?
studentTasks: Memorize ينمو as the four-letter group.
Mark the target, word boundary, and trigger.
Contrast one izhar example with one idgham example.
Recite one verified example for each trigger.
independentPractice: Review ينمو and the four verified boundaries.
Mark target, boundary, and trigger before reciting.
homework: Prepare four teacher-approved examples, one for each letter.
For each example: identify, explain, count two, then recite to the teacher.
exitTicket: Explain why فَمَن يَعْمَلْ uses idgham with ghunnah.
Recite one selected example with controlled two-count ghunnah.
masteryCriteria: Names all four letters without prompting.
Identifies the rule in at least 8 of 10 mixed boundaries.
Explains that the rule occurs across two words.
Merges without a separate noon sound.
teacherNotes: Recognition, merging, and timing are separate mastery targets.
Do not teach the absolute-manifestation exceptions as ordinary idgham; they are the next lesson.
A written shaddah may help the learner see the result, but teacher listening remains essential.
Use the same decision routine established in the foundations lesson.
